summary: Entry was flat at t=0, dipped -19.75pts by t=1m which I held as normal noise. By t=2m price accelerated to -59.5pts (3x the prior dip in one minute), both HA and PROPP fire signals flipped from with/mixed to against, and leg giveback collapsed to 0% -- i.e. the adverse move stopped mean-reverting and was extending cleanly against the position. That combination (accelerating adverse velocity + both directional fires against + zero giveback) read as wrong-direction, not a normal dip, so I bailed at frame 2. Next time I'd watch giveback% specifically: high giveback on an adverse leg (like the initial 53-62%) signals the counter-move is itself fading and the position may recover, while a drop to 0% giveback alongside multiple against-fires is the tell that the adverse leg is now the dominant, persisting move.
